Decision_Register.title: Canonical ownership
Decision_Register.decision: M00 owns identity and session context, authorization decisions, shared configuration, feature controls, consent decisions, audit and event envelopes, integration context, task foundation, secrets references, environment controls, and release controls. M05 owns Tenant, Organization, and OrganizationRelationship. M04 owns MarketplaceContext, branding, product visibility, attribution, and marketplace routing. M00 may expose read models and shared administration components but shall not create competing canonical stores.

Decision_Register.title: Lucie tenant model
Decision_Register.decision: A tenant is the primary security and data-isolation boundary, not a synonym for agency. Lucie supports one JET internal tenant and one tenant per onboarded commercial customer or agency group, with multiple organizations and agency downlines inside the tenant. Nested tenants, self-service tenant creation, and cross-tenant organization hierarchies are excluded.

Decision_Register.title: Tenant provisioning
Decision_Register.decision: Only a JET Platform Administrator may provision a tenant. Required inputs are display name, owning organization, internal reference code, lifecycle status, default marketplace reference, effective date, and approved commercial activation status. Automated onboarding, subscription billing, deployment-region selection, self-service activation, and customer-managed infrastructure are excluded.

Decision_Register.title: Tenant lifecycle
Decision_Register.decision: Use fixed tenant states DRAFT, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, and ENDED. Only ACTIVE tenants may initiate normal production activity. SUSPENDED tenants cannot start new sessions or transactions, while authorized JET administrators retain historical access. ENDED tenants are retained for audit and reporting and cannot be reactivated without a controlled administrative decision.

Decision_Register.title: Organization types
Decision_Register.decision: Use the fixed organization types JET_PLATFORM, AGENCY, EMPLOYER, CARRIER, VENDOR, and PARTNER. Downline status is represented by relationship, not a separate organization type. Custom organization types are excluded. Carrier, vendor, and partner records may initially be reference-only.

Decision_Register.title: Organization relationships
Decision_Register.decision: Lucie exposes one simple effective-dated parent/downline hierarchy. Each agency may have at most one active parent at a time, using the fixed relationship type PARENT_OF. Multiple parents, arbitrary relationship graphs, delegation workflows, contract sharing, revenue sharing, and visual graph editing are excluded. Contracts remain versioned for future expansion.

Decision_Register.title: Tenant owner
Decision_Register.decision: Every tenant has exactly one owning organization. Agency-customer tenants are owned by the primary agency and the JET internal tenant is owned by JET. Ownership changes are controlled JET administrative actions requiring reason, audit evidence, and effective date.

Decision_Register.title: Marketplace model
Decision_Register.decision: Each tenant has one active production marketplace in Lucie. The marketplace contains references for brand/theme, supported channel, product visibility policy, routing policy, attribution, and disclosures. JET has a JET marketplace and each agency customer may have one agency-branded marketplace. Nested marketplaces, networks, storefront builders, and multiple concurrent production storefronts per tenant are excluded. M04 owns marketplace editing.

Decision_Register.title: Marketplace resolution
Decision_Register.decision: Public storefronts resolve MarketplaceContext from a JET-controlled hostname or route mapping. The server derives the associated tenant and owning organization; client-supplied context cannot override it. Unknown, suspended, expired, or invalid marketplace resolution fails closed with a controlled unavailable state and never silently falls back to another marketplace.

Decision_Register.title: Required active context
Decision_Register.decision: Every protected request must resolve user_id, session_id, actor_type, tenant_id, organization_id, marketplace_id, role_assignment_id, affiliation_id when applicable, authentication_strength, policy_version, and correlation_id on the server. Missing, inconsistent, expired, or unauthorized context is denied; unrestricted wildcard context is prohibited.

Decision_Register.title: Consumer identity across marketplaces
Decision_Register.decision: Use one global consumer identity and login. Consumer business records remain scoped to the tenant and marketplace where created. Households, quotes, applications, and documents are not automatically merged across tenants. Cross-context sharing occurs only through an explicit, authorized, audited share or handoff mechanism.

Decision_Register.title: Workforce identity and membership
Decision_Register.decision: Use one global workforce identity with tenant-scoped memberships and role assignments. A Lucie agent operates under one primary active agency affiliation at a time. Agency administrators and unlicensed staff are limited to authorized tenant and organization scope. JET Platform Administrators may hold platform scope. End-user management of multiple active producer affiliations and complex inheritance is excluded.

Decision_Register.title: Context switching
Decision_Register.decision: JET Platform Administrators may explicitly switch tenant and marketplace context. Each switch must show a persistent active-context banner, validate server-side, create an audit record, clear incompatible cached state, and require explicit target selection. Agency users cannot switch tenants. Consumers change marketplace by entering another approved storefront and must see its active brand.

Decision_Register.title: Cross-tenant access
Decision_Register.decision: Normal Lucie workflows may not directly read or modify another tenant's data. Authorized aggregate reporting uses a separate data pipeline rather than broad application queries. Temporary JET support access must be explicit, reason-coded, time-limited, permission-controlled, and audited.

Decision_Register.title: Canonical identifiers
Decision_Register.decision: Use server-generated UUID version 4 identifiers for canonical records. IDs are opaque, globally unique, never reused, independent of names or business meaning, and transported consistently as strings. Separate human-readable reference codes may be shown to administrators. API and schema fields use lowercase snake_case.

Decision_Register.title: Versioning and effective dates
Decision_Register.decision: Use simple record versioning, not a generalized temporal engine. Material records include integer version, effective_from, optional effective_to, created_at, created_by, updated_at, and updated_by. Timestamps use UTC ISO 8601. Relationship, configuration, marketplace, and authorization evidence preserve prior versions; normal corrections still generate audit history.

Decision_Register.title: Historical transaction reconstruction
Decision_Register.decision: Material transactions store canonical context IDs and the relevant configuration, policy, product, consent, and marketplace version references used at the time. Immutable snapshots are created only where reconstruction requires them, including quotes, applications, signed outputs, and formal handoffs. The platform does not copy every context object into every transaction.

Decision_Register.title: M00 administration boundary
Decision_Register.decision: M00 delivers the shared platform administration shell, context selector and banner, context validation components, tenant/organization/marketplace summary cards, contract-backed read models, status/dependency indicators, common authorization, and audit behavior. M05 later delivers tenant/organization/relationship workflows; M04 later delivers marketplace/branding/visibility/attribution/routing workflows. M00 may use approved fixtures or mocks but may not create temporary competing canonical schemas.

Decision_Register.title: Seed data
Decision_Register.decision: Nonproduction environments receive one JET tenant, organization, and marketplace; one synthetic agency tenant, agency organization, downline agency, and agency marketplace; and representative users for each Lucie role. Production begins only with JET records and explicitly approved customer records. Launch customer, carrier, state, legal entity, and vendor decisions are not hardcoded.

Decision_Register.title: Context security test baseline
Decision_Register.decision: Every protected API and sensitive screen must test valid active context, missing context, wrong tenant, wrong marketplace, unauthorized organization, suspended tenant, suspended marketplace, expired membership, stale relationship or affiliation, client context tampering, explicitly scoped JET administration, and audit evidence for privileged attempts.

Decision_Register.title: Future compatibility boundary
Decision_Register.decision: Contracts preserve identifiers, versions, ownership boundaries, and adapters needed later for multiple marketplaces, richer organization graphs, multiple agent affiliations, dedicated deployment models, and broader relationship types. Lucie does not build their screens, workflows, configuration editors, or operational logic.

Decision_Register.title: Identity ownership
Decision_Register.decision: M00 owns global user identity, authentication, contact verification, account status, sessions, multifactor authentication, recovery, permission definitions, role assignment envelopes, access decisions, privileged access controls, and authentication/authorization audit events. M06 owns agency, agent, staff profiles and affiliations. M08 owns licenses, appointments, credentials, captive restrictions, and sellability. M00 consumes downstream decisions without duplicating canonical data.

Decision_Register.title: Global user identity
Decision_Register.decision: Each person receives one global server-generated user_id. A single identity may have workforce, consumer, and employer-contact actor profiles. The system shall not create a second identity merely because the person enters through another marketplace and shall not auto-merge records based only on matching email or telephone.

Decision_Register.title: Authentication service
Decision_Register.decision: Use one managed standards-based identity service supporting OpenID Connect or equivalent. ABox shall not build a custom password engine. The service provides secure credential storage, email and telephone verification, OTP, password recovery, MFA, session revocation, brute-force controls, token rotation, and authentication history. Social login, enterprise SSO, SAML, SCIM, bring-your-own identity provider, and selectable providers are future seams.

Decision_Register.title: Consumer authentication
Decision_Register.decision: Consumers may browse, enter basic quote information, and view public product content anonymously. Authentication is required to save/resume, retain a household, share a quote, receive protected documents, start an application, use electronic signature, complete a formal external handoff, or access prior records. Supported methods are verified email/password and verified telephone OTP, with at least one verified contact method before full activation.

Decision_Register.title: Workforce authentication
Decision_Register.decision: All workforce accounts are invitation-only. JET administrators, agency administrators, selling agents, and unlicensed staff must verify the invited email, establish credentials, enroll in MFA, accept applicable terms/privacy notice, and enter only authorized tenant and organization context. Open workforce registration and tenant discovery are excluded.

Decision_Register.title: Employer contact authentication
Decision_Register.decision: Employer contacts use a verified account tied to an explicit employer organization, created by authorized invitation or controlled ICHRA quote initiation. They cannot search for, join, or administer arbitrary employers. M20 owns employer workflows; M00 provides identity and access foundations.

Decision_Register.title: Multifactor authentication
Decision_Register.decision: MFA is mandatory for every workforce user, using authenticator-app time-limited codes through the managed identity service and one-time recovery codes. Consumer and employer accounts do not require routine MFA but may require OTP or recent authentication for sensitive actions. SMS cannot be the only factor for privileged JET administration. No configurable MFA policy designer is included.

Decision_Register.title: Fixed role templates
Decision_Register.decision: Lucie supports six fixed role templates: JET_PLATFORM_ADMIN, AGENCY_ADMIN, SELLING_AGENT, UNLICENSED_STAFF, CONSUMER, and EMPLOYER_CONTACT. Custom roles, custom permission bundles, role designers, agency-authored policies, and tenant-specific role taxonomies are excluded. Permissions remain individually defined beneath the fixed templates.

Decision_Register.title: Multiple workforce roles
Decision_Register.decision: A workforce identity may hold multiple fixed roles where necessary, commonly AGENCY_ADMIN plus SELLING_AGENT. Permissions may be additive, but explicit restrictions, tenant and organization scope, affiliation status, and sellability decisions prevail. Administrative status does not itself authorize regulated selling.

Decision_Register.title: Role assignment authority
Decision_Register.decision: JET Platform Administrators may assign any Lucie role in authorized context. Agency Administrators may invite/manage users in their agency and permitted downlines and assign AGENCY_ADMIN, SELLING_AGENT, or UNLICENSED_STAFF. They cannot create JET admins, grant cross-tenant access, override failed sellability, grant outside their hierarchy, change permission definitions, or reactivate a platform-suspended identity. All changes are audited.

Decision_Register.title: Permission model
Decision_Register.decision: Use a fixed server-side permission catalogue with resource.action identifiers such as user.invite, quote.read, application.submit, tenant.configure, audit.read, and integration.test. Every protected operation evaluates permission server-side. UI hiding or disabling is informative only. Access is denied unless explicitly permitted.

Decision_Register.title: Authorization inputs
Decision_Register.decision: Authorization uses server-resolved active context plus actor type, fixed roles, tenant and organization membership, marketplace, record ownership/assignment, agency affiliation, current sellability where applicable, account status, tenant and marketplace status, authentication strength, and recent authentication for sensitive actions. Client-supplied role or context cannot grant access.

Decision_Register.title: Consumer record access
Decision_Register.decision: Consumers may access only their own identity, household, quotes, carts, applications, documents, communications, and handoff records. Agents and staff need explicit assignment, agency relationship, shared quote, assistance event, or takeover authorization. Ordinary agents do not receive an unrestricted tenant-wide consumer directory. Assistance and takeover preserve actor attribution.

Decision_Register.title: Selling authority boundary
Decision_Register.decision: M00 enforces access to selling actions but does not calculate legal sellability. M08 returns reason-coded ALLOWED, BLOCKED, REVIEW_REQUIRED, or NOT_APPLICABLE. If M08 is unavailable, stale, or indeterminate, regulated selling fails closed while permitted nonselling support may continue.

Decision_Register.title: Account lifecycle
Decision_Register.decision: Use fixed account states PENDING_VERIFICATION, ACTIVE, LOCKED, SUSPENDED, and ENDED, and invitation states PENDING, ACCEPTED, EXPIRED, and REVOKED. Locked accounts may recover; suspended accounts require authorized administration; ended accounts preserve historical IDs and cannot sign in. IDs are never reused.

Decision_Register.title: Session controls
Decision_Register.decision: Use secure HTTP-only same-site cookies; authentication tokens are not stored in browser local storage. Workforce sessions last at most eight hours with a 30-minute inactivity timeout, no remember-me, and reauthentication after account, role, or affiliation changes. Consumer/employer sessions may be remembered up to 30 days; sensitive actions require recent authentication; sign-out terminates the current session and sign-out-all-devices is available. Access tokens are short-lived and refresh tokens rotate.

Decision_Register.title: Step-up authentication
Decision_Register.decision: Require recent authentication or MFA confirmation before password/contact changes, MFA reset, privileged role changes, tenant suspension/ending, secret access, emergency access, sensitive export, electronic signature, regulated submission, or external enrollment handoff. Step-up validity is at most 15 minutes. No configurable step-up policy engine is required.

Decision_Register.title: Password and account recovery
Decision_Register.decision: Recovery is self-service through verified email or telephone. Links/codes are single-use, time-limited, rate-limited, invalidated after use, and excluded from logs/analytics. Administrators may trigger recovery or revoke sessions but cannot view passwords, set permanent passwords, read OTPs, or bypass verification. Successful recovery revokes existing sessions and creates audit evidence.

Decision_Register.title: Authentication abuse controls
Decision_Register.decision: Use managed identity protections for rate limiting, progressive delay, suspicious-login detection, temporary lockout, OTP attempt limits, credential-stuffing controls, and breached-password detection where supported. Authentication and recovery responses do not reveal whether an account exists. CAPTCHA may be risk-triggered but is not required on every login. A custom fraud platform is excluded.

Decision_Register.title: Account administration screens
Decision_Register.decision: M00 provides authorized user search, user summary, invitation creation/resend, fixed-role assignment, activation/suspension, MFA reset, session revocation, last successful sign-in, recent access history, and effective memberships. Custom permission editing, identity graphs, enterprise directory sync, device-fingerprint investigation, behavioral risk scoring, and agency identity-provider configuration are excluded. Agency roster and producer detail remain M06.

Decision_Register.title: JET support and emergency access
Decision_Register.decision: Only specifically authorized JET Platform Administrators may initiate emergency access. It requires target tenant, reason code, written justification, incident/support reference where available, maximum 60-minute duration, read-only default, persistent banner, automatic expiry, and complete audit. Write access requires separate permission and additional reason. Sensitive values remain masked unless explicitly essential. No standing cross-tenant browser is created.

Decision_Register.title: User impersonation
Decision_Register.decision: Production login-as-user functionality is prohibited. JET administrators inspect through their own audited identity and explicit tenant context. Nonproduction may use role preview with synthetic users and data. No production session may inherit or conceal another person's identity.

Decision_Register.title: Service identities
Decision_Register.decision: Background jobs, internal services, and integrations use dedicated workload identities with named owner, purpose, least privileges, environment restriction, credential rotation, revocation, and authentication audit. Shared human accounts are prohibited. Secrets live in the approved secrets service, not source code, database rows, browser code, logs, or documentation.

Decision_Register.title: Sensitive identity data
Decision_Register.decision: Passwords, OTPs, recovery/session tokens, MFA secrets, and integration credentials are never displayed after creation and never appear in logs, URLs, analytics, errors, support exports, or audit payloads. M00 provides a shared PII/regulated-data masking framework; downstream modules classify their fields and use the shared mechanism.

Decision_Register.title: Required identity audit events
Decision_Register.decision: Audit registration, invitations, verification success/failure, login success/failure, logout, session revocation, recovery, password change, MFA enrollment/reset, account lock/suspension/ending, role and membership changes, context switch, authorization denial, sensitive-data access, emergency access, and service-identity authentication failure. Credentials and tokens are excluded.

Decision_Register.title: Identity and access acceptance baseline
Decision_Register.decision: Automated acceptance must cover consumer registration/verification, workforce invitation/MFA, recovery success and failure, suspended/ended denial, dynamic role changes, wrong tenant/organization/marketplace denial, consumer ownership, unlicensed staff restrictions, failed sellability denial, client tampering denial, session timeout/revocation, step-up, emergency-access expiry, production impersonation absence, credential-free logs, and required audit events. These become shared downstream regression obligations.

Decision_Register.topic: Commercial Activation, Entitlements, Feature Controls and Workspace Experience
Decision_Register.title: Selected commercial availability
Decision_Register.decision: Lucie is available only to tenants explicitly activated by JET. Tenant creation alone does not create commercial availability. Production use requires active tenant status, active commercial activation, at least one entitled product line, an active marketplace, satisfied launch gates, and required downstream product/integration readiness. Public tenant registration, automatic trials, and general-availability enrollment are excluded.

Decision_Register.topic: Commercial Activation, Entitlements, Feature Controls and Workspace Experience
Decision_Register.title: Commercial activation authority
Decision_Register.decision: Only a JET Platform Administrator may activate, suspend, or end commercial access. Agency Administrators may view status, effective dates, enabled product lines/channels, workforce seat allocation, and usage but cannot alter contractual entitlements or activate products.

Decision_Register.topic: Commercial Activation, Entitlements, Feature Controls and Workspace Experience
Decision_Register.title: Commercial activation record
Decision_Register.decision: Each customer tenant has one current commercial activation record with internal agreement reference, status, effective start, optional end, enabled product lines, enabled channels, workforce seat allocation, internal notes, creator/approver, and change history. Subscription plans, automated pricing, invoicing, coupons, usage billing, contract authoring, and automatic renewal are outside Lucie; agreements and invoicing are handled externally.

Decision_Register.topic: Commercial Activation, Entitlements, Feature Controls and Workspace Experience
Decision_Register.title: Commercial activation lifecycle
Decision_Register.decision: Use fixed commercial states PENDING, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, and ENDED. PENDING permits setup/testing but not production customer activity. ACTIVE permits entitled production activity when all gates pass. SUSPENDED blocks new commercial activity while preserving records. ENDED permanently closes activation while retaining history. Technical tenant administration may remain available separately.

Decision_Register.topic: Commercial Activation, Entitlements, Feature Controls and Workspace Experience
Decision_Register.title: Product-line entitlements
Decision_Register.decision: Use fixed entitlements IFP_ON_EXCHANGE, IFP_OFF_EXCHANGE, DENTAL, VISION, and ICHRA_EMPLOYER_QUOTING, enabled separately per tenant. Custom product-line categories are excluded. Entitlement grants commercial permission only; real availability still depends on data, geography, carrier setup, legal approval, sellability, and launch gates.

Decision_Register.topic: Commercial Activation, Entitlements, Feature Controls and Workspace Experience
Decision_Register.title: Channel entitlements
Decision_Register.decision: Use fixed channels CONSUMER_DIRECT, AGENT, and EMPLOYER. Agent initiation, assistance, and takeover are behaviors inside AGENT. IFP, dental, and vision may use consumer-direct and agent; ICHRA employer quoting may use employer and agent. Each tenant receives only approved channels. Custom channels are excluded.

Decision_Register.topic: Commercial Activation, Entitlements, Feature Controls and Workspace Experience
Decision_Register.title: Workforce seat allocation
Decision_Register.decision: Each commercial tenant has one workforce-seat allocation covering active Agency Administrators, Selling Agents, and Unlicensed Staff. JET admins do not consume seats. Pending invitations consume no seat until acceptance; acceptance is blocked if allocation would be exceeded. Only JET may change allocations. Temporary overages and automated seat purchase are excluded.

Decision_Register.topic: Commercial Activation, Entitlements, Feature Controls and Workspace Experience
Decision_Register.title: Usage visibility
Decision_Register.decision: Provide operational usage visibility for active seats, pending invitations, quotes started/saved, applications initiated/submitted/handed off, documents generated, PlanAI sessions, outbound communications, and external handoffs. M00 may show basic counts and allocations; M24 owns richer analytics. Counts do not generate invoices or change entitlements automatically.

Decision_Register.topic: Commercial Activation, Entitlements, Feature Controls and Workspace Experience
Decision_Register.title: Entitlements, feature controls and launch gates
Decision_Register.decision: Treat entitlement, feature control, and launch gate as separate decisions. Entitlement means commercial permission; feature control means technical enablement; launch gate means legal, security, operational, data, product, and integration readiness. A capability is available only when every applicable control permits it.

Decision_Register.topic: Commercial Activation, Entitlements, Feature Controls and Workspace Experience
Decision_Register.title: Feature-control ownership
Decision_Register.decision: JET alone creates and manages a predefined feature catalogue. Production targeting is limited to environment, all Lucie tenants, selected tenant, or named launch cohort. User targeting, percentage rollout, behavioral rules, custom expressions, agency controls, and a general experimentation platform are excluded, while contracts may preserve future targeting.

Decision_Register.topic: Commercial Activation, Entitlements, Feature Controls and Workspace Experience
Decision_Register.title: Emergency capability controls
Decision_Register.decision: JET receives predefined emergency disable controls for new quote initiation, PlanAI, application submission, JET EDE handoff, carrier submission, electronic signature, outbound email, outbound SMS, document generation, and payment simulation. Disablement prevents new actions without deleting completed work. Changes require reason and audit, not a configurable approval workflow.

Decision_Register.topic: Commercial Activation, Entitlements, Feature Controls and Workspace Experience
Decision_Register.title: Configuration ownership and precedence
Decision_Register.decision: Use a controlled hierarchy: JET platform default, permitted tenant override, M04-owned marketplace setting, and permitted user preference. Not every setting is overridable. JET controls platform and tenant configuration; M04 controls branding/visibility/attribution/routing; agencies receive only explicit business settings. A generic configuration editor or unrestricted inheritance/rules engine is excluded.

Decision_Register.topic: Commercial Activation, Entitlements, Feature Controls and Workspace Experience
Decision_Register.title: Workspace model
Decision_Register.decision: Lucie uses six fixed workspaces determined by actor, role, entitlement, and status: JET Platform Administration, Agency Administration, Agent Workspace, Consumer Shopping, Member Workspace, and Employer Quoting. Member Workspace is available for consumers with authoritative confirmed enrollment and uses the same global identity. It provides enrollment/application status, selected-plan summary, confirmation or handoff reference, effective date when available, documents, messages, next actions, preferences, prior journey history, and support contacts. Full policy servicing, claims, billing, ID cards, policy changes, and renewal management remain future seams. Workspace builders, custom navigation/routes, drag-and-drop menus, agency dashboards, and per-user menu design are excluded.
Decision_Register.amendment: Supersedes the original five-workspace recommendation by adding Member Workspace.

Decision_Register.topic: Commercial Activation, Entitlements, Feature Controls and Workspace Experience
Decision_Register.title: Navigation behavior
Decision_Register.decision: Navigation is generated from the fixed Lucie IA. Ordinary users do not see unavailable modules in primary navigation; direct links show a controlled unavailable message without internal security/configuration details. JET admins may see disabled capabilities and the entitlement, feature, gate, or dependency blocking them.

Decision_Register.topic: Commercial Activation, Entitlements, Feature Controls and Workspace Experience
Decision_Register.title: Landing-page preferences
Decision_Register.decision: Each role has a default landing page: Platform Home for JET admin, Agency My Work for agency admin, Agent My Work for selling agent and unlicensed staff, most recent active shopping journey for consumer, Member Workspace landing for enrolled members, and most recent employer quote/start for employer contact. Users may choose only from a short permitted list. Agencies cannot design landing pages.

Decision_Register.topic: Commercial Activation, Entitlements, Feature Controls and Workspace Experience
Decision_Register.title: Language posture
Decision_Register.decision: Lucie supports English and Spanish. English is default. A language picker is available throughout; authenticated preference is stored in the user profile and applied across devices/sessions. Anonymous preference persists through the journey and transfers on registration. The selected language applies to navigation, forms, validation, consent/disclosures, help, transactional email/SMS, in-app notifications, generated documents, PlanAI interactions, and all workspaces. Regulated, legal, carrier, and product content is enabled in Spanish only after an approved version exists; no automatic machine translation of regulated content. Prior evidence remains tied to its original language/version.

Decision_Register.topic: Commercial Activation, Entitlements, Feature Controls and Workspace Experience
Decision_Register.title: Geography reference model
Decision_Register.decision: Lucie supports the United States only. M00 provides versioned reference data for the United States, states, District of Columbia, and applicable territories retained for reference. JET does not create custom countries, states, or regions. Actual product availability is limited to approved launch states through product, marketplace, legal, and sellability controls. The launch-state list is a production activation input, not an M00 discovery blocker.

Decision_Register.topic: Commercial Activation, Entitlements, Feature Controls and Workspace Experience
Decision_Register.title: Configuration changes
Decision_Register.decision: Configuration and activation changes are versioned and audited. Most approved changes take effect immediately after confirmation. Commercial activation/ending, product-line changes, marketplace activation, state activation, and major integration cutover may be future-effective. No generic configuration approval engine is included; launch gates and emergency access retain controlled processes.

Decision_Register.topic: Commercial Activation, Entitlements, Feature Controls and Workspace Experience
Decision_Register.title: Agency-controlled settings
Decision_Register.decision: Agency Administrators may manage workforce invitations within seat limits, fixed roles within authority, permitted landing preferences, organization notification defaults where permitted, and user activation/suspension within scope. They may view but not modify entitlements, launch gates, feature controls, platform configuration, secrets, legal/privacy classification, or emergency controls. M04 later provides limited branding/presentation settings.

Decision_Register.topic: Commercial Activation, Entitlements, Feature Controls and Workspace Experience
Decision_Register.title: Protected M01 continuity
Decision_Register.decision: M01 shopping and JET EDE handoff remain available only when tenant, marketplace, product, geography, feature, and launch controls permit. M00 does not alter M01 identifiers or silently change behavior. Every impact creates an M01 impact record and proposed delta with before/after behavior, compatibility, regression, UI/terminology, and release-note treatment. New artifacts use canonical PlanAI while historical terms remain traceable.

Decision_Register.topic: Consent, Privacy, Member Records and Audit
Decision_Register.title: Consent catalogue
Decision_Register.decision: Use a fixed JET-controlled catalogue for terms of use, privacy notice, electronic communications, transactional SMS, marketing email, marketing SMS, agent assistance/record access, external sharing/handoff, electronic signature, and PlanAI disclosure. Consents are purpose-specific. Agencies cannot create custom consent types or combine all permissions into a blanket consent.

Decision_Register.topic: Consent, Privacy, Member Records and Audit
Decision_Register.title: Required and optional choices
Decision_Register.decision: Clearly distinguish transaction-required consent/acknowledgement, optional marketing consent, optional communication preferences, and optional assistance/sharing permissions. Optional choices are never preselected. Declining marketing cannot block shopping, applying, required transactional communications, or Member Workspace access.

Decision_Register.topic: Consent, Privacy, Member Records and Audit
Decision_Register.title: Consent timing
Decision_Register.decision: Request consent at the point it becomes relevant: terms/privacy at registration, SMS before first SMS, agent access before assistance/takeover, sharing before external handoff, e-sign consent before signing, and PlanAI disclosure before first interaction and after a material change. Do not repeat unchanged consent unless expired, revoked, or materially revised.

Decision_Register.topic: Consent, Privacy, Member Records and Audit
Decision_Register.title: Language and version of consent
Decision_Register.decision: Present consent in the user's selected English or Spanish language and retain language, exact text/document version, purpose, channel, actor, time, tenant, marketplace, collection method, related transaction, and revocation history. Users may switch before accepting; later language changes do not rewrite prior evidence. Material changes require renewed acceptance where required.

Decision_Register.topic: Consent, Privacy, Member Records and Audit
Decision_Register.title: Agent-assisted consent
Decision_Register.decision: Agents/staff may guide the consumer, send a secure consent link, or record legally permitted verbal consent. Verbal evidence records consumer, agent, approved script version, time, communication method, purpose, and response. Agents cannot silently accept digital consent for consumers. Direct consumer action remains required for e-signatures, regulated attestations, and similar actions unless an approved representative process applies.

Decision_Register.topic: Consent, Privacy, Member Records and Audit
Decision_Register.title: Household members and authorized representation
Decision_Register.decision: A primary subscriber may enter household/dependent data and complete application activities for adults in the same eligible household. Where the destination permits a household application filer, the primary subscriber may complete and sign one household submission with evidence identifying performer, represented adults, certification, application version, time, language, and destination. Where separate authorization is required, the primary subscriber may propose themselves as authorized representative and the adult may approve through a secure link and one-time verification without creating a full account. Evidence records represented adult, representative, fixed scope, effective date, revocation, language/version, and authentication method. Existing legal authority such as guardianship or power of attorney may be recorded. Minors do not receive independent accounts. A general-purpose power-of-attorney system, representative hierarchies, multiple simultaneous representatives, custom scopes, and automated legal-document validation are excluded. Destination rules remain authoritative and direct adult action is required when mandated.
Decision_Register.amendment: Supersedes the original recommendation that every adult must always act personally by adding destination-aware household filer and authorized representative paths.

Decision_Register.topic: Consent, Privacy, Member Records and Audit
Decision_Register.title: Agent access to consumer records
Decision_Register.decision: Agent access requires an explicit relationship: consumer-selected assistance, approved sharing, lead assignment, agency-created journey, authorized takeover, or application assignment. Consumer approval is required when consumer-direct activity changes to agent-assisted access. Access is limited to relevant records and purpose and does not grant permanent access to future activity.

Decision_Register.topic: Consent, Privacy, Member Records and Audit
Decision_Register.title: External sharing and handoff
Decision_Register.decision: Point-in-time authorization must identify destination, information shared, purpose, copy/referral/formal-handoff nature, next step, access expiry if any, and support route. Material destination, purpose, or data changes require new authorization. General Lucie consent does not authorize unrelated handoffs.

Decision_Register.topic: Consent, Privacy, Member Records and Audit
Decision_Register.title: Consent withdrawal
Decision_Register.decision: Withdrawal applies prospectively: stop future optional marketing, sharing, and new agent access covered by the consent; preserve original consent/withdrawal evidence, completed transactions, handoffs, and legally required records. Required security, application, and enrollment messages may continue. Explain what will and will not stop before confirmation.

Decision_Register.topic: Consent, Privacy, Member Records and Audit
Decision_Register.title: Member Workspace activation
Decision_Register.decision: Member Workspace is activated only after authoritative confirmed-enrollment evidence from JET EDE, carrier, approved enrollment result, or authorized JET operational confirmation supported by external evidence. Saved plan, cart, started/submitted application, initiated handoff, or pending outcome does not create member status. A consumer may access both shopping and member areas through one account.

Decision_Register.topic: Consent, Privacy, Member Records and Audit
Decision_Register.title: Member record scope
Decision_Register.decision: The MVP member record is a read-oriented enrollment summary, not policy administration. It may include consumer/household reference, selected product/plan, enrollment status, application/handoff reference, carrier/destination, confirmation reference, effective date, documents, contacts, outstanding actions, source, and last update. Clearly identify externally sourced information and authoritative support party. Do not imply ABox is the policy-administration system.

Decision_Register.topic: Consent, Privacy, Member Records and Audit
Decision_Register.title: Corrections and historical records
Decision_Register.decision: Current profile, contact, preference, and household data may be corrected where allowed. Submitted applications, signed documents, quotes, consent evidence, and completed handoffs are not overwritten. Corrections affecting submitted/signed transactions create a new version, amendment/correction record, linkage to prior version, updated status/next action, and audit evidence.

Decision_Register.topic: Consent, Privacy, Member Records and Audit
Decision_Register.title: Privacy requests
Decision_Register.decision: Consumers, members, employer contacts, and workforce users may request access, correction, portability where applicable, account closure, deletion where legally available, and usage/sharing explanation. Provide a simple request form and status. JET manages a small queue with SUBMITTED, IN_REVIEW, COMPLETED, and DENIED; denial requires a user-visible reason where appropriate. Broad privacy case management is excluded.

Decision_Register.topic: Consent, Privacy, Member Records and Audit
Decision_Register.title: Account closure
Decision_Register.decision: Consumers/members may request closure from settings. Closure ends sessions, prevents sign-in, stops optional marketing, preserves required transaction/audit/enrollment evidence, warns about active applications or handoffs, and explains that closure is neither coverage cancellation nor automatic legal deletion. Workforce accounts are ended administratively.

Decision_Register.topic: Consent, Privacy, Member Records and Audit
Decision_Register.title: Retention and deletion posture
Decision_Register.decision: JET controls retention by data type, transaction, legal/contractual obligations, and legal holds. Agencies/users cannot create schedules. Eligible data may be deleted or de-identified while preserving required audit, consent, signed/submitted transaction evidence, legal-hold information, and nonidentifying metrics. Distinguish closure, deletion, archival, and de-identification.

Decision_Register.topic: Consent, Privacy, Member Records and Audit
Decision_Register.title: Sensitive-data visibility
Decision_Register.decision: Sensitive data is masked by default. Full values are visible only to the subject or an authorized user with a permitted need, within the required workflow, for the minimum time. Lists, search, notifications, ordinary exports, support views, and analytics do not show full sensitive identifiers. Emergency access does not automatically unmask. Reveal actions are permission-controlled and audited.

Decision_Register.topic: Consent, Privacy, Member Records and Audit
Decision_Register.title: Audit access
Decision_Register.decision: Audit records are immutable through application screens. JET admins may search authorized platform/tenant activity; agency admins may review relevant activity in their hierarchy; ordinary workforce users see activity tied to themselves and assigned work; consumers/members see simplified account activity; employer contacts see their account/employer quote activity. User views include sign-ins, contact changes, consent/withdrawal, agent sharing, applications/signatures, handoffs, closure, and privacy requests without exposing internal security signals or other users.

Decision_Register.topic: Consent, Privacy, Member Records and Audit
Decision_Register.title: Audit exports
Decision_Register.decision: JET admins may export filtered audit evidence for approved investigation, compliance, legal, or support purposes, requiring tenant scope, date range, purpose, reason, requester, and an audit record of the export. Agency admins do not receive unrestricted bulk audit export in the MVP. Consumers/members may download simplified activity and privacy results.

Decision_Register.topic: Consent, Privacy, Member Records and Audit
Decision_Register.title: Legal holds
Decision_Register.decision: JET may place a legal hold on tenant, user, household, application/enrollment, document, handoff, or another identified record set. Holds prevent deletion while allowing authorized access as appropriate and record reason, owner, start date, optional review date, and release history. Full e-discovery is outside scope.

Decision_Register.topic: Consent, Privacy, Member Records and Audit
Decision_Register.title: Tenant privacy classification
Decision_Register.decision: Every production tenant receives a JET-controlled classification: STANDARD, BAA_OR_ENHANCED_CONTROLS_REQUIRED, or PENDING_LEGAL_REVIEW. Pending legal review blocks production. Agencies may view operational requirements but cannot alter classification. Exact legal and BAA determination is a production gate.

Decision_Register.topic: Consent, Privacy, Member Records and Audit
Decision_Register.title: M01 continuity
Decision_Register.decision: Review M01 impacts to registration/authentication, global identity, consumer dashboard/Member Workspace, English/Spanish, language persistence, consent/disclosures, agent assistance/takeover, sharing, JET EDE authorization, privacy/closure, masking, audit, and post-handoff/enrollment status. Classify each impact as no change, clarification, compatible addition, behavior revision, UI/terminology revision, data/contract migration, or regression-only. Preserve M01 IDs and require traceable proposed deltas.

Decision_Register.title: Shared work model
Decision_Register.decision: M00 provides one simple shared work model for tasks, alerts, exceptions, narrowly defined approvals, external follow-ups, and consumer/employer next actions. A general-purpose workflow platform, process designer, case-management suite, and configurable business-process engine are excluded.

Decision_Register.title: My Work experience
Decision_Register.decision: Every workforce workspace includes a fixed My Work page with Assigned to me, Assigned to my permitted team, Due soon, Overdue, Blocked, Recently completed, and Items requiring consumer/external action. Users may filter by status, due date, work type, module, and assignee. User-designed views, custom dashboards, arbitrary saved queries, and configurable queues are excluded.

Decision_Register.title: Consumer and member next actions
Decision_Register.decision: Consumer Shopping and Member Workspace show a simple Next Actions section for verification, household completion, quote review, agent access, representation authorization, document upload, signature, enrollment result review, inconsistency resolution, external contact, and privacy responses. Internal JET/agency tasks are never exposed.

Decision_Register.title: Task creation
Decision_Register.decision: Tasks may be created by a user, predefined Lucie workflow, downstream module, integration result, failed/incomplete automation, or authorized administrator. Task types are predefined; tenants/agencies cannot create custom types, forms, or rules. Controlled free-text title and notes are permitted.

Decision_Register.title: Task assignment
Decision_Register.decision: Tasks may be assigned to a named workforce user, fixed operational team, consumer, employer contact, JET operations, responsible agency, or originating system awaiting response. Agency admins may reassign only within permitted hierarchy; JET may reassign across authorized Lucie contexts; consumers/employers cannot reassign internal workforce work.

Decision_Register.title: Operational teams
Decision_Register.decision: Use fixed team types JET_PLATFORM_OPERATIONS, JET_COMPLIANCE_REVIEW, JET_INTEGRATION_SUPPORT, AGENCY_ADMINISTRATION, AGENCY_SALES, and AGENCY_SUPPORT. Tenants may map users to these teams but cannot create new team types in the MVP. A user may belong to multiple teams.

Decision_Register.title: Task lifecycle
Decision_Register.decision: Use fixed task states OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, WAITING_ON_CONSUMER, WAITING_ON_EXTERNAL_PARTY, BLOCKED, and COMPLETED. Completed work may reopen only if related work is not final or a new actionable condition occurs. Custom statuses are excluded.

Decision_Register.title: Priority and due dates
Decision_Register.decision: Use NORMAL, HIGH, and URGENT priorities. Most work is NORMAL. Due dates are calculated by predefined rules or selected by authorized users. URGENT is reserved for time-sensitive enrollment, compliance, security, or customer-impacting work. Customer-authored SLAs and complex scoring formulas are excluded.

Decision_Register.title: Reminders and escalation
Decision_Register.decision: Provide predefined reminders for Due soon, Due today, Overdue, and Overdue escalation. Default escalation is assigned user, responsible team, then agency administrator or JET owner based on ownership. Consumer reminders use in-app, email, or SMS according to consent/preferences. No graphical escalation-rule builder.

Decision_Register.title: Exception model
Decision_Register.decision: An exception represents a condition preventing or materially risking workflow completion, including missing data, identity failure, unavailable product data, failed sellability, missing signature/authorization, handoff failure, enrollment mismatch, document failure, timeout, or privacy/legal-hold conflict. Each exception has fixed type, severity, related record, responsible module, owner, user-safe explanation, internal diagnostic reference, and resolution status.

Decision_Register.title: User-facing error treatment
Decision_Register.decision: Distinguish user-correctable validation, temporary system problem, external-party delay, blocked compliance/authorization, and internal operational exception. Show clear next steps without stack traces, vendor payloads, security details, or confidential notes. Preserve valid entered information whenever possible.

Decision_Register.title: Manual resolution
Decision_Register.decision: Authorized users may resolve exceptions using predefined actions: correct, request information, retry, reassign, record external outcome, confirm evidence, cancel affected action, mark duplicate, or close with reason. Administrators cannot rewrite transaction history or mark an externally failed enrollment successful without authoritative evidence.

Decision_Register.title: Manual override
Decision_Register.decision: There is no universal override. Downstream modules may define a specific override only where business/compliance rules permit. Each override requires permission, fixed reason, explanation, before/after value, actor, time, evidence, and audit. License, appointment, identity, consent, signature, and authoritative enrollment failures cannot be overridden for convenience.

Decision_Register.title: Approval posture
Decision_Register.decision: No generalized approval engine. Approvals are limited to production tenant activation, marketplace activation, production integration cutover, launch-gate completion, high-risk export, emergency write access, and legal-hold release. Ordinary tasks, invitations, agency assignments, quote activity, and standard configuration changes do not need multistep approval.

Decision_Register.title: Comments and internal notes
Decision_Register.decision: Workforce users may add immutable internal notes to tasks/exceptions. Notes identify author/time, are hidden from consumers/employers, may be corrected only by follow-up note, and cannot contain credentials or unnecessary sensitive data. Consumer/employer communication uses a separate user-facing message.

Decision_Register.title: Attachments
Decision_Register.decision: Tasks/exceptions link to documents stored through M13's shared document service rather than a separate attachment store. Uploads use approved flows with validation, malware scanning, classification, access control, retention, and audit. M13 remains canonical owner.

Decision_Register.title: Duplicate work prevention
Decision_Register.decision: When the same unresolved task/exception would be generated again for the same related record, type, and responsible module, update the existing item rather than duplicate it. Authorized users may create another item only for genuinely separate work.

Decision_Register.title: Work history
Decision_Register.decision: Every task/exception retains chronological read-only history of creation, assignment, status, priority, due date, comments, retry, resolution, reopen, and completion, linked to platform audit. Consumers see only simplified history relevant to their own actions.

Decision_Register.title: Operational search
Decision_Register.decision: Authorized workforce search supports work reference, consumer/member name, application/quote reference, organization, assignee, work type, status, and date range. Sensitive IDs are not the normal search key and remain masked. Search is restricted to authorized tenant and organization context.

Decision_Register.title: M01 continuity
Decision_Register.decision: Review M01 impacts for save/resume, abandonment, assistance requests, takeover, missing application data, consumer authorization, signature, JET EDE status/failure/delay, enrollment confirmation, consumer/member next actions, English/Spanish reminders, and PlanAI follow-up. M01 should consume shared task/exception contracts where appropriate; changes require protected deltas and cumulative regression.

Decision_Register.title: Integration control plane ownership
Decision_Register.decision: M00 owns connector registry, environment/activation context, credential references, connector lifecycle/health, shared background jobs, retry/reconciliation controls, webhook/callback monitoring, integration audit, and common failure handling. Domain modules own business meaning, mappings, validation, and outcomes. M00 does not duplicate quote, application, product, license, communication, or enrollment truth.

Decision_Register.title: Fixed Lucie connector catalogue
Decision_Register.decision: Use a small JET-controlled catalogue for JET EDE, Ideon product/plan data, NIPR or another approved licensing provider, Twilio SMS, DocuSign electronic signature, a JET-approved secure email service and gateway, PlanAI runtime, and approved carrier application output through API, EDI, SFTP, or document pathways. Implement and activate only connectors required by an enabled Lucie pathway. Generic connector builders, tenant-authored integrations, arbitrary endpoints, user-defined mapping, public integration marketplace, and multiple interchangeable providers are excluded.

Decision_Register.title: Provider account ownership and commercial sourcing
Decision_Register.decision: For Twilio SMS, DocuSign electronic signature, and approved secure email/gateway, each agency chooses independently between AGENCY_OWNED and JET_PAY_TO_USE. Under agency-owned, the agency owns the provider agreement/license and capacity; JET securely configures and operates the ABox connection, never redisplays credentials, and may suspend invalid or noncompliant connections. Under JET pay-to-use, JET owns the provider account, attributes usage by tenant/service/transaction/date/marketplace/outcome, and handles charges through the commercial agreement without an automated billing engine. Each tenant has one active production route per service. Model changes are controlled, future-effective where necessary, tested, audited, protect in-flight transactions, and preserve historical provider association. If no route is active, dependent functionality remains unavailable and never silently uses JET paid capacity.
Decision_Register.amendment: Supersedes prior Lucie assumptions of JET-only SendGrid and JET E-Signature.

Decision_Register.title: Integration administration authority
Decision_Register.decision: Only JET admins may create approved connector instances, enter/replace credential references, test, activate/suspend, change endpoints, reconcile, retry, or retire. Agency admins see simplified availability/delay/unavailable/pending status for their tenant but never credentials, full payloads, other tenants, internal diagnostics, or provider-wide configuration.

Decision_Register.title: Connector lifecycle
Decision_Register.decision: Use lifecycle states DRAFT, TESTING, READY, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, and RETIRED, plus health HEALTHY, DEGRADED, UNAVAILABLE, and UNKNOWN. Activation requires applicable legal, security, data, operational, and provider-certification gates. Suspension blocks new activity while preserving history and authorized reconciliation.

Decision_Register.title: Environment model
Decision_Register.decision: Use four controlled environments: LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT, QA, UAT, and PRODUCTION. Local development uses synthetic data, mocks/emulators, or provider sandboxes and never production data/credentials. QA supports automated functional, integration, security, regression, accessibility, and failure testing with synthetic data. UAT supports product, operations, agency, and business acceptance with approved test accounts and provider sandbox/certification connections, including complete English/Spanish journeys. Production uses separately controlled live credentials, data, activation, monitoring, and access. No implicit sharing of credentials, endpoints, data, or activation state across environments; agency-specific sandboxes and customer-controlled promotion are excluded.

Decision_Register.title: Nonproduction simulations
Decision_Register.decision: Local, QA, and UAT support predefined success, pending, validation failure, provider rejection, temporary outage, timeout, duplicate callback, delayed callback, partial response, and unmatched response simulations. Simulations are clearly labeled and cannot create production enrollment, messages, signatures, license results, or submissions. Production never substitutes simulated success for unavailable providers.

Decision_Register.title: Connector activation scope
Decision_Register.decision: Prefer one JET-managed provider connector per environment, with availability enabled for approved tenant, marketplace, product line, carrier pathway, launch state, or cohort. Agencies cannot create duplicate instances. Platform-active does not imply availability to every tenant or pathway.

Decision_Register.title: Scheduled integration activity
Decision_Register.decision: Connectors may run on predefined JET schedules. JET admins may view, pause, resume, run an approved job immediately, and see last/next run. No general schedule designer, custom cron expressions, or agency-defined schedules. The owning domain defines allowed schedule options.

Decision_Register.title: External outage behavior
Decision_Register.decision: Preserve completed work and distinguish saved-not-sent, queued for safe retry, sent/pending, rejected, and manual-action-required. Safe actions may queue; authoritative decisions fail closed or remain pending rather than assume success. No automatic provider switching.

Decision_Register.title: Retry and replay
Decision_Register.decision: Automatic retries occur only for idempotent or otherwise safe actions. JET may manually retry/replay an approved failed action using the original immutable request version. Payloads cannot be edited and resent as the same transaction; corrections create a linked new version/submission. Prevent duplicate external actions wherever provider contracts permit.

Decision_Register.title: Reconciliation
Decision_Register.decision: Reconcile pending, incomplete, or inconsistent external transactions on schedule, after delayed callbacks/outages, or on JET demand. Authoritative results update the owning-domain status. Conflicts create an exception and preserve prior status/evidence; no silent overwrite of a final user-visible outcome. Each domain defines its authoritative source.

Decision_Register.title: Webhooks and callbacks
Decision_Register.decision: Valid callbacks are matched to an existing request, deduplicated after recording, preserve original context, record provider outcome, update user-visible status, and create an exception when unmatched or unprocessable. JET sees a safe operational summary/history, not unrestricted raw sensitive payloads or credentials.

Decision_Register.title: Shared manual-import experience
Decision_Register.decision: All structured manual imports use a fixed CSV experience: download approved template, populate permitted fields, upload, validate entire file, review summary, commit, and download result/error report. Domain modules own columns and rules; M00 owns shared job framework. User-defined columns, mapping, formulas, macros, arbitrary sheets, transformation rules, and generic migration tools are excluded.

Decision_Register.title: Import commit behavior
Decision_Register.decision: Manual CSV imports commit all-or-nothing. Any blocking row error prevents all records from committing and produces a row-level error report; corrected files may be re-uploaded and failed attempts remain in history. Nonblocking warnings may be acknowledged before commit. Partial-success files are excluded.

Decision_Register.title: Export posture
Decision_Register.decision: Authorized users may perform on-demand CSV exports only from approved lists, within visible tenant/organization scope, approved fields, masking/privacy controls, and stated operational purpose. JET may export broader evidence when separately authorized. Scheduled reports belong to M24. Generic database dumps and unrestricted exports are excluded.

Decision_Register.title: Background-job visibility and cancellation
Decision_Register.decision: Use QUEUED, RUNNING, WAITING_ON_EXTERNAL_PARTY, COMPLETED, COMPLETED_WITH_WARNINGS, FAILED, and CANCELED. Authorized users see jobs they initiated or operate. Cancellation is allowed only before irreversible external action; after submission, use withdrawal/correction/follow-up. Consumers/employers see business status, not technical terminology.

Decision_Register.title: External-data provenance and correction
Decision_Register.decision: External data retains provider, source record/transaction reference, received time, mapping version, data version where available, last successful refresh, status, and connector/job references. Generic administration cannot silently overwrite external values. Permitted corrections use owner-domain workflows preserving original/corrected value, reason, actor, and evidence.

Decision_Register.title: Platform operations experience
Decision_Register.decision: JET Platform Administration shows connector lifecycle/health, last success/failure, pending/failed jobs, open integration exceptions, delayed callbacks, environment, tenant/pathway impact, retry/reconciliation actions, and launch-gate status. Critical failures alert the accountable JET owner. User-built dashboards, custom alert builders, infrastructure consoles, direct database access, generic API clients, payload editing, and support backdoors are excluded.

Decision_Register.title: Protected M01 integration continuity
Decision_Register.decision: Review M01 INT-001 through INT-018 and related JET EDE, product data, PlanAI, identity context, communications, consent, geography, audit, status/retry, and monitoring against the M00 control plane. Preserve M1D-017, M1D-024, and M1D-025 links and create/extend deltas for Spanish, Member Workspace, household representation, callbacks, outages, and provider routing. Compatibility adapters may preserve M01 behavior without replacing IDs or evidence.

Decision_Register.topic: Release Controls, Acceptance, Support and Delta Closure
Decision_Register.title: M00 delivery boundary
Decision_Register.decision: M00 delivers shared shell/navigation, English/Spanish framework, global identity/authentication, context enforcement, fixed roles/permissions, commercial activation/entitlements, feature/emergency controls, consent/audit, shared work, integration control plane, import/export foundation, provider sourcing/usage attribution, platform administration, operational health, and release controls. It does not implement complete downstream business functionality. Member Workspace shell/status are M00; application/enrollment data comes from M26 and integrations; policy servicing remains M18.

Decision_Register.topic: Release Controls, Acceptance, Support and Delta Closure
Decision_Register.title: Lean MVP scope rule
Decision_Register.decision: A capability belongs in M00 only when multiple modules need it, it is essential for security/privacy/audit/isolation/production, it is necessary to launch protected M01 safely, separate implementations would conflict, or a future seam must be preserved. Phase 1/North Star presence alone is not sufficient. Favor fixed roles/workspaces/statuses, predefined providers, small configuration sets, JET-operated administration, and explicit seams; exclude general-purpose designers, policy/workflow engines, custom taxonomies, arbitrary integrations, and customer-authored platform behavior.

Decision_Register.topic: Release Controls, Acceptance, Support and Delta Closure
Decision_Register.title: Deployment and activation separation
Decision_Register.decision: Code deployment does not expose a capability. Availability requires deployed approved version, ready environment, active tenant/commercial activation, entitlements, provider readiness, launch gates, explicit feature enablement, and tenant/cohort activation.

Decision_Register.topic: Release Controls, Acceptance, Support and Delta Closure
Decision_Register.title: Initial production rollout
Decision_Register.decision: Use a controlled rollout: JET internal production validation, one selected pilot agency, a small approved cohort, then tenant-by-tenant activation. Pilot identity may be selected later and is not hardcoded. Each tenant passes its own activation, provider, branding, entitlement, legal, product-data, and operational readiness. No automatic broad launch.

Decision_Register.topic: Release Controls, Acceptance, Support and Delta Closure
Decision_Register.title: Production launch gates
Decision_Register.decision: Production activation requires applicable evidence for product scope, security/privacy, tenant/marketplace configuration, commercial activation, English/Spanish content, legal/regulated language, accessibility, provider connections, product/geography data, M01 continuity/regression, UAT, monitoring, support ownership, incident/rollback procedures, training/handoff, and no release-blocking defect. A nonapplicable gate requires rationale.

Decision_Register.topic: Release Controls, Acceptance, Support and Delta Closure
Decision_Register.title: Go or no-go authority
Decision_Register.decision: JET owns final production go/no-go. One named JET Release Owner records the decision after evidence from product, engineering, QA, security/privacy, legal/compliance where applicable, platform operations, business operations, integration owners, and pilot/customer representative where applicable. No complex voting workflow.

Decision_Register.topic: Release Controls, Acceptance, Support and Delta Closure
Decision_Register.title: UAT ownership
Decision_Register.decision: JET owns formal UAT with representative JET admins, agency admins, selling agents, unlicensed staff, consumers, enrolled members, employer contacts where applicable, and JET operations. Pilot agencies validate agency workflows before activation. Consumer/member journeys are tested in English and Spanish. Results record user, scenario, environment, result, evidence, and accepted limitations.

Decision_Register.topic: Release Controls, Acceptance, Support and Delta Closure
Decision_Register.title: English and Spanish release parity
Decision_Register.decision: A user-facing capability is production-ready only when English and Spanish are complete for the activated pathway, including screens, validation, help, consent/disclosures, notifications, secure email, SMS, generated documents, signing instructions, PlanAI, errors, and next actions. Regulated production content is not machine translated. A capability may be disabled for Spanish only if it is not exposed to Spanish users and approved handling prevents incomplete English-only transactions.

Decision_Register.topic: Release Controls, Acceptance, Support and Delta Closure
Decision_Register.title: Provider readiness and commercial routing
Decision_Register.decision: Each tenant has an approved route per provider-dependent feature: AGENCY_OWNED, JET_PAY_TO_USE, or NOT_ENABLED for Twilio, DocuSign, and secure email gateway. JET validates commercial model, account status, environment setup, sender/brand, testing, consent/templates, callbacks/delivery, usage attribution, support ownership, and suspension. License purchase alone is insufficient.

Decision_Register.topic: Release Controls, Acceptance, Support and Delta Closure
Decision_Register.title: Pay-to-use measurement
Decision_Register.decision: JET pay-to-use activity records tenant, marketplace, service, transaction type, time, quantity, outcome, business reference, and reversal/cancellation where applicable. Agency admins see summarized usage but not JET costs or other tenants. JET may export usage for external invoicing/reconciliation. Lucie does not calculate tax, invoice, collect payment, or manage collections.

Decision_Register.topic: Release Controls, Acceptance, Support and Delta Closure
Decision_Register.title: M01 protected-release gate
Decision_Register.decision: M00 cannot be production-approved until each M01 impact is classified as no change, clarification, compatible addition, UI/terminology revision, behavioral revision, contract/data migration, regression-only, or deferred dependency. Each proposed change includes existing reference, current/proposed behavior, reason, owner, compatibility, data/UI/language/test/release-note treatment, approval, and implementation status. Original M01 IDs/evidence are preserved.

Decision_Register.topic: Release Controls, Acceptance, Support and Delta Closure
Decision_Register.title: M01 delta packaging
Decision_Register.decision: The M00 packet includes a dedicated M01 area with prior delivered module impact register, M01 continuity review, proposed deltas, affected requirements/screens/workflows/contracts/events, terminology including PlanAI, English/Spanish impacts, compatibility/migration, cumulative regression, open decisions, and implementation-ready instructions. Approved deltas are append-only and later modules add to the same companion.

Decision_Register.topic: Release Controls, Acceptance, Support and Delta Closure
Decision_Register.title: Release rollback and emergency disable
Decision_Register.decision: Support safe code/configuration rollback and immediate feature/provider disable. Rollback cannot delete completed work/audit, silently reverse handoffs/messages/submissions/signatures/enrollment, or overwrite authoritative results. In-flight activity remains visible and is reconciled. JET may stop new activity while preserving existing records and user-safe status.

Decision_Register.topic: Release Controls, Acceptance, Support and Delta Closure
Decision_Register.title: Defect severity
Decision_Register.decision: Use CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, and LOW. Critical blocks release for cross-tenant access, unauthorized access, data loss, incorrect enrollment/submission, invalid signature/consent evidence, sensitive-data exposure, incorrect regulated selling, production-wide outage, or audit corruption. High blocks affected capability unless safely disabled. Medium/low may be accepted with owner and resolution plan.

Decision_Register.topic: Release Controls, Acceptance, Support and Delta Closure
Decision_Register.title: Support ownership
Decision_Register.decision: For agency-branded marketplaces the agency is first contact for ordinary consumer/member/agent help; JET handles platform, identity, integration, security, and unresolved defects and may provide direct support by agreement. JET is first contact for the JET marketplace. Carrier, Exchange, employer, and provider issues route to the authoritative external party. Users always see a context-, language-, and workflow-appropriate support route.

Decision_Register.topic: Release Controls, Acceptance, Support and Delta Closure
Decision_Register.title: Incident communication
Decision_Register.decision: Provide predefined workspace banners, consumer/member unavailable messages, agency-admin notices, JET alerts, email/SMS where permitted, and status updates tied to affected work. State affected capability, whether work is safe, retry behavior, next action, and support contact. Do not expose infrastructure/security details, raw payloads, or uncertain promises.

Decision_Register.topic: Release Controls, Acceptance, Support and Delta Closure
Decision_Register.title: Tenant suspension and offboarding
Decision_Register.decision: On suspension/ending, block new activity as appropriate, protect records, reconcile in-flight transactions, disable agency-owned connections after transition, stop JET pay-to-use except where needed to complete/document existing work, produce authorized exports, apply consumer/member continuity, and retain required evidence. Offboarding is JET-controlled; legally required records cannot be deleted on demand.

Decision_Register.topic: Release Controls, Acceptance, Support and Delta Closure
Decision_Register.title: Legacy and data migration posture
Decision_Register.decision: M00 excludes a general legacy migration program. It supports JET seed data, approved tenant onboarding, M01 identifier/data compatibility, controlled reference and workforce imports, required configuration migration, and M01 delta-driven corrections. Broader historical/customer migration requires separate scope and acceptance.

Decision_Register.topic: Release Controls, Acceptance, Support and Delta Closure
Decision_Register.title: Operational handover
Decision_Register.decision: Production approval requires an executable handover covering supported functionality, limitations, tenant/provider activation, environments, user/role administration, monitoring, retry/reconciliation, emergency disable, incidents, support routing, common failures, export/offboarding, M01 continuity, and English/Spanish support. Operations must not depend on undocumented engineering knowledge.

Decision_Register.topic: Release Controls, Acceptance, Support and Delta Closure
Decision_Register.title: Build-packet completion standard
Decision_Register.decision: The M00 packet is complete only when an AI-assisted engineering team can implement, test, deploy, and operate without material product inference. Include controlled scope/exclusions, numbered requirements/rules, roles/permissions, UI specs, English/Spanish, ownership/data/API/event/integration contracts, work/exception behavior, security/privacy/audit, acceptance/tests/regression, environments/deployment, runbook, prior-module impacts, M01 deltas, traceability workbook, machine registry, manifest/checksums, and QA/self-audit. IDs remain stable.

Decision_Register.topic: Release Controls, Acceptance, Support and Delta Closure
Decision_Register.title: Change control after discovery lock
Decision_Register.decision: After discovery lock, behavioral change enters through a numbered change record identifying original requirement, proposed change, reason, affected screens/contracts, M01 and downstream impacts, compatibility, tests, approval, and target packet version. Editorial corrections may not change meaning and still preserve IDs and version history.

Decision_Register.topic: Release Controls, Acceptance, Support and Delta Closure
Decision_Register.title: Discovery closure
Decision_Register.decision: Topic 7 approval closes M00 functional discovery. Packet authoring uses all Topic 1-7 decisions, Lucie handover, dependency analysis, protected M01 baseline and cumulative deltas, modern enterprise SaaS standards, and the lean-MVP rule. Launch customer, provider account, legal classification, state activation, and production credential details are controlled activation inputs, not blockers to packet authoring.

Requirement_Register.title: Canonical ownership
Requirement_Register.statement: M00 owns identity and session context, authorization decisions, shared configuration, feature controls, consent decisions, audit and event envelopes, integration context, task foundation, secrets references, environment controls, and release controls. M05 owns Tenant, Organization, and OrganizationRelationship. M04 owns MarketplaceContext, branding, product visibility, attribution, and marketplace routing. M00 may expose read models and shared administration components but shall not create competing canonical stores.

Requirement_Register.title: Lucie tenant model
Requirement_Register.statement: A tenant is the primary security and data-isolation boundary, not a synonym for agency. Lucie supports one JET internal tenant and one tenant per onboarded commercial customer or agency group, with multiple organizations and agency downlines inside the tenant. Nested tenants, self-service tenant creation, and cross-tenant organization hierarchies are excluded.

Requirement_Register.title: Tenant provisioning
Requirement_Register.statement: Only a JET Platform Administrator may provision a tenant. Required inputs are display name, owning organization, internal reference code, lifecycle status, default marketplace reference, effective date, and approved commercial activation status. Automated onboarding, subscription billing, deployment-region selection, self-service activation, and customer-managed infrastructure are excluded.

Requirement_Register.title: Tenant lifecycle
Requirement_Register.statement: Use fixed tenant states DRAFT, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, and ENDED. Only ACTIVE tenants may initiate normal production activity. SUSPENDED tenants cannot start new sessions or transactions, while authorized JET administrators retain historical access. ENDED tenants are retained for audit and reporting and cannot be reactivated without a controlled administrative decision.

Requirement_Register.title: Organization types
Requirement_Register.statement: Use the fixed organization types JET_PLATFORM, AGENCY, EMPLOYER, CARRIER, VENDOR, and PARTNER. Downline status is represented by relationship, not a separate organization type. Custom organization types are excluded. Carrier, vendor, and partner records may initially be reference-only.

Requirement_Register.title: Organization relationships
Requirement_Register.statement: Lucie exposes one simple effective-dated parent/downline hierarchy. Each agency may have at most one active parent at a time, using the fixed relationship type PARENT_OF. Multiple parents, arbitrary relationship graphs, delegation workflows, contract sharing, revenue sharing, and visual graph editing are excluded. Contracts remain versioned for future expansion.

Requirement_Register.title: Tenant owner
Requirement_Register.statement: Every tenant has exactly one owning organization. Agency-customer tenants are owned by the primary agency and the JET internal tenant is owned by JET. Ownership changes are controlled JET administrative actions requiring reason, audit evidence, and effective date.

Requirement_Register.title: Marketplace model
Requirement_Register.statement: Each tenant has one active production marketplace in Lucie.
